title: Request-Reply

validation.research: Six primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Request-Reply, Return Address, and Correlation Identifier catalogs; RabbitMQ RPC tutorial; NATS request-reply documentation; and AWS timeout/retry guidance. The article distinguishes logical request/reply paths from physical connections, blocking from callback handling, return routing from correlation, application results from receipt acknowledgments, local timeout from remote cancellation, and correlation from server-side idempotency. Request-Response and Request/Reply are aliases; no duplicate entry was found.

example_limits: Original sequential trusted-envelope inventory conversation using a dictionary of reply inboxes and manual message delivery. Stock counts are units observed from a fixed teaching inventory, not reservations. Requestor owns up to two pending product/deadline contexts, generates session-prefixed sequence IDs, accepts matching replies strictly before a local deadline, returns the original product context, ignores unmatched or duplicate replies, and removes expired entries explicitly. Time uses nonnegative nondecreasing integer milliseconds. Session freshness across delayed replies/restarts is a stated assumption. Expiration neither cancels nor rolls back remote work. No broker, network, untrusted payload validator, persistence, retry, business idempotency, synchronization, durable continuation, lifecycle scheduler, authentication, or restart recovery; transport queues are not bounded by the pending limit. NATS is an explanatory second context only.
